title: Whether a provider credential follows a per-call url, in three languages
pins: Whether the credential a provider was configured with is SENT when a per-call url points it somewhere else, and whether a provider name can be registered over one already taken. Both cross a language boundary because the configuration is shared: the same OPENAI_API_KEY and the same gateway url are handed to a PHP app and to a TypeScript or Python agent, so a url that receives the key in one language and not the others leaks it in whichever got it wrong, and nothing errors to say so. What a consumer loses when this drifts is the credential itself. Registration is the same story one level down: a factory registered over `openai` receives every caller's openai traffic. Since 0.1.27 it also pins named OpenAI-compatible providers (G-321 A): a configured entry with driver openai-compatible must authenticate with its own key and nothing else, so an OPENAI_* value reaching a vLLM or gateway host is the same leak one level up, and a compatible entry under a built-in name is the same shadowing. The chat-completions request body those entries send (G-321 D, ported to TypeScript and Python) is compared byte for byte.
scope: OpenAI, Anthropic and Mistral only, the three providers every language ships. The reference's other fifteen providers, its configured-credential keys beyond api_key/organization/project (access_token, credentials_path) and Vertex region validation are covered by the reference's own regression test, not here. Streaming, embeddings and every other entry point share the constructor these rows exercise but are not dispatched here. Observations classify the wire; they do not record which host the request reached. Compatible rows (kind compatible) configure one entry the way each language does it — PHP config prism.providers.<name>, TypeScript configureProviders(), Python configure_providers() — and observe one text, structured, stream or tool call. They do not observe response parsing, tool loops or approvals, which the ports implement differently from the reference and say so in their own tests.
construction: Native PHP manager entered through Prism::text()->using() with Laravel's HTTP fake and stray requests prevented; native TypeScript Prism.text().using() with fetch captured; native Python Prism.text().using() with the default transport's send captured and sockets refused. Every fixture answers 500, because only the outgoing request matters. Environment values are synthetic and isolated per row; PHP reads them through the package's own config file, as an application does. Every observation is a classification of the captured URL, headers and body — inherited, explicit, both or none — and never the value: tools/credential-scope/contract.mjs refuses an observation that carries a fixture credential. Compatible rows run each TypeScript observation in a process of its own, because configureProviders() registers process-wide and has no undo; Python restores its registry between rows; PHP builds a fresh manager. Their observation adds the refusal class (matched on the stable phrase each language shares), whether any Authorization header was sent, the target (entry url, api.openai.com or other), the path, the canonical request body, and whether the error chain carries a fixture credential.
findings: 62 of 62 rows agree, recorded against the G-321 A+D branches of prism, prism-ts and prism-py (24 compatible rows, cs-0039..cs-0062). Every compatible row agrees: a compatible entry sends only its own key to its own url; with no key or an empty key there is no Authorization header in any language although OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_ORGANIZATION and OPENAI_PROJECT are all set; a private address and the link-local metadata address are dispatched (provider urls carry no address policy, a decision recorded in the gaps register) and receive no foreign credential; openai and OpenAI as compatible names are refused as collisions, a padded name and a Cyrillic look-alike as invalid names; file, missing and padded urls, an unknown api format and an unknown driver are refused before any request; a per-call url elsewhere drops the entry key; an unreachable endpoint fails without the key in any error; and the text, stream, structured and tool chat-completions bodies are identical in all three. The bodies agree on the reference's own quirks too — a stream and a structured body send max_tokens as null, a stream sends no stream_options, structured output is a json_object plus an appended system message — which is agreement with the reference, not a claim that those choices are right. The earlier rows: Every endpoint row agrees, including the hostile ones: a port, scheme, path, query or userinfo change, the trusted host spelled as userinfo, a backslash the parsers read differently, and a Cyrillic homoglyph host all drop the inherited key in all three; trailing slash, case and the explicit default port keep it in all three; the environment key is bound to the environment url, not to the provider default. A url carrying whitespace or a control character anywhere (cs-0016) is refused before any request in all three. It used to be the one row that disagreed, and not on purpose: TypeScript and Python trimmed the padded url and sent the inherited key to the trusted host, while PHP's verdict moved with its HTTP stack (refused under Guzzle 8, sent under Guzzle 7). Refusal is the answer that does not depend on a library, and the PHP runner is now locked (runners/php/composer.lock) so no verdict here can drift with a dependency release. Registration agrees on every row: a provider name must match the ASCII allow-list ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$ in all three, so padded, zero-width, Cyrillic-homoglyph (cs-0037) and full-width (cs-0038) look-alikes of `openai` are refused and the built-ins still resolve afterwards; collisions are ASCII case-insensitive, so `OpenAI`, `ANTHROPIC` and a case variant of an earlier custom name are refused everywhere. The allow-list replaced a forbidden-character test that leaned on each language's Unicode tables, which is where the languages disagree. That agreement is a conclusion about behaviour, not about safety: the three were written to one spec at the same time, so a shared misreading of it would agree here too. The observations are those of the fix branches; released versions are expected not to match them until those ship.

discrimination.gap: No mutation probe is delivered for this suite. Released versions predating the fix branches are expected to fail it, which serves as a coarse negative control.

php.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with php --check; it dispatches to the native PHP adapter. PRISM_AUTOLOAD points it at a checkout instead of runners/php.

ts.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with ts --check; it reads the built sibling prism-ts/dist, or PRISM_TS_DIST.

py.note: Run the corpus-loading entry point with py --check; it imports the installed package, or PRISM_PY_SRC.
